about.title: Cupertino Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Cupertino's public-record crash data shows two traffic deaths in the most recent final year, alongside 160 injury collisions across corridors like I-280, De Anza Boulevard, Stevens Creek Boulevard, and SR-85. Behind each number is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss. California law gives close family members, and in some cases other dependents, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with real deadlines and rules about who may file. If someone in your life was killed in a Cupertino-area crash, an independent attorney can review what happened, explain the timeline you're working with, and help you understand what losses the law allows a family to recover. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply help connect grieving families with attorneys who focus on this kind of case, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Start

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with certain other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. An attorney can clarify where you fit before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity is involved. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. A civil claim is separate from any criminal case tied to the same crash.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim after a Cupertino crash?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of death to file. If the crash involved a government vehicle or roadway defect, the deadline is often much shorter, so it's worth speaking with an attorney early.

items.question: Can extended family members file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Priority goes to a spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing, but the rules are specific. An attorney can review your situation and explain where you stand.

items.question: Does De Anza Boulevard or Stevens Creek Boulevard being high-volume corridors affect our case?
items.answer: Public crash-count data for corridors like De Anza Boulevard and Stevens Creek Boulevard can help establish context around where a crash occurred, but every case turns on its own facts. An attorney reviewing the specific collision report will know what matters most.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensating the family, regardless of what happens in a criminal case. The two proceedings run independently and follow different rules and timelines.
